content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no MFN obligation burdens Sparkling.

I checked the sections where an MFN would plausibly live and ran targeted text searches:

- **Fees (sec-11, p0084)** — a bare payment obligation: Sparkling pays the amounts in the Fee Schedule. No pricing-comparison or matching mechanic.
- **Maintenance and Support (sec-10)** — maintenance pricing simply cross-refers to the Fee Schedule; no benchmarking against other customers or third-party offers.
- **General Matters (sec-20)** — only time of the essence and notices.
- **Searches** for "most favoured nation", "no less favourable", "favourable/favorable", "best price", "lowest", "other customers", "discount" and "third party" surfaced nothing relevant (the only "third party" hits are confidentiality and assignment; the only "best" hits are best-efforts obligations, one of which runs against Garman).

This sits at the **preferred position** — no MFN obligation on the Customer — so no redline was proposed.

One note flagged in the rationale rather than as a deviation: the agreement contains **no MFN in our favour either**. That is outside this rule's scope (the rule only guards against MFNs running against us), but it is available as a commercial ask if the deal team wants Garman to commit to best pricing on the Fee Schedule.
